[CONDITION_REMOVED:Bloodied Nose]
[COMPANION_CONDITION_REMOVED:Daeris|Unconscious]
[COMPANION_CONDITION_REMOVED:Daeris|Traumatized]

The nose stopped hurting somewhere on the stairs. You didn't notice when.

The man doesn't look dead. Doesn't look right either. Slumped against the terminus stone with his chin on his chest. Breathing. Shallow. Slow. The green light catches the hollows of his face.

Thin. Very thin. The kind of thin that takes months.

You shape the Message. Send it quiet into the cave.

*Can you hear me?*

Nothing for a long moment.

Then his head moves. Fraction of an inch. Like the sound reached somewhere deep and took time travelling back up.

His mouth opens.

The reply comes back through the cantrip. Barely a whisper. Cracked at the edges.

*Still here.*

Two words. That's all.

Frizwick makes a sound beside you. Not quite a word.

Morwen's hand finds the back of your arm. Steady.

The man's eyes open. Wrong colour. Should be brown or green or grey. They're faintly luminous instead. The same shade as the channels upstairs. Blue-white at the rim.

He's been down here a long time.

The mechanism has been keeping him company.

[QUEST_STEP:Aldus Vareth|Reach Aldus Vareth and assess his condition|true]
[QUEST:Aldus Vareth|completed]
[XP:300]

You hold up a fist. Stop.

Frizwick freezes. Morwen too.

You scan.

[DICE:Perception check|18|success]
[SKILL_SUCCESS:Perception]

The cave is big enough to swallow sound. Tidal pools along the eastern wall, still and dark. A natural chimney above that lets in a thread of grey sky. Two crevices in the north face, deep enough to hide something. The terminus stone itself, carved and massive, older than everything above it.

Nothing moves.

No breath but yours and his. No sound but the sea working at the rock outside. The green light is steady. Not pulsing. Not reacting.

The mechanism isn't alarmed.

That's something.

You move forward. Slow. One hand near a blade. Eyes on the crevices.

Nothing comes out.

Aldus Vareth doesn't move until you're four feet away. Then one hand lifts. Weak. Halfway. Falls back.

Up close he's worse. The eyes aren't just luminous at the rim. The colour bleeds through the iris when the light catches it. Like something seeped in over two years and didn't leave.

His lips move. No cantrip needed now. You're close enough to hear.

"You're real," he says. Flat. Like he stopped trusting that distinction some time ago.

You crouch beside him. Don't touch him yet.

The terminus stone is enormous up close. Chest height sitting down. The spiral rune matches your disc exactly, line for line. Not similar. Identical.

You pull the disc from your pocket and hold it near the surface.

[DICE:Arcana check|19|success]

The stone reacts.

Not dramatically. No light show. No sound. But the carved lines nearest the disc deepen slightly in colour. The faintest brightening. A recognition response. Like a lock acknowledging a key that wasn't meant for this door.

The script around the spiral is different from the channel walls above. Older. Less regular. This predates the harvest mechanism. The mechanism was built around this stone, not the other way around.

Aldus has been sitting against the receiving end of ten thousand years of accumulated resonance.

Not stored here. Passing through.

The reservoir drains into this stone and the stone does something with it. Disperses it. Into the sea, maybe. Into the rock. The terminus isn't a container.

It's a drain.

You look at Aldus. At his eyes.

The mechanism kept him alive because he's been sitting in the outflow. Whatever pours through here poured through him too. Sustained him. Changed him.

He's watching you examine the stone.

"It hums," he says quietly. "You stop hearing it after a while."

You look at his hands first. Habit.

No wounds. No cuts, no healed-over damage. Fingernails grown out long and then worn back down again. The hands of someone who had nothing to do for a very long time.

You check his neck. His arms. Pull back the collar of a coat that's mostly held together by memory. No marks. No lesions. No sign of the cave taking anything from him physically.

[DICE:First Aid check|15|success]
[SKILL_SUCCESS:First Aid]

Muscle loss. Significant. Whatever the mechanism fed him kept him breathing but not strong. His legs when you press them are thin as rope. Standing will be a project.

His temperature is wrong. Not fever. Not cold. Something between the two that doesn't have a name. Like the stone behind him has been sharing its temperature with him. Whatever that means.

His breathing is slow. Steady. Too steady. Too regular. Healthy people breathe unevenly. Aldus breathes like a mechanism.

But no infection. No rot. No starvation damage despite two years without a proper meal.

The drain kept him. Incidentally. As a side effect of proximity.

Morwen crouches on his other side. Studies his face.

"Pupils respond," she says quietly. "That's something."

Frizwick stands behind you both. Arms folded. Not saying what she's thinking.

His eyes track you. Blue-white at the rim. Waiting.

"Can you stand?"

He considers it seriously. Like it's a complicated question.

"Don't know," he says. "Haven't tried."

Fair answer.

You get a hand under his arm. Morwen takes the other side. His weight is less than it should be for a man his size. The muscle loss is worse than it looked. You feel the bones of his shoulder clearly through the ruined coat.

You lift.

He gets his feet under him. Shaking. Bad. His legs remember the general idea of standing without committing to it.

[DICE:Constitution check — Aldus|8|failed]

His knees go.

You catch him. Morwen catches him. He doesn't go down but it's close.

He stays upright. Held mostly by the two of you. Breathing hard from four seconds of effort.

"Stairs," Frizwick says from behind. Not a question. An observation about the problem ahead.

Aldus looks at the terminus stone. The stone he hasn't moved from in two years. His expression does something complicated.

"I thought about walking," he says. "Made plans. Routes. Which way the stairs would be." He pauses. "Counted steps from the stone twice a day so I wouldn't forget the distance."

He looks at you.

"Is Corven still alive?"

You jerk your chin at Frizwick. Then at Aldus.

She's already moving.

No complaint. No comment. She gets under his other arm without being asked twice, swaps with Morwen, and takes his weight with the practiced ease of someone who's carried people out of bad places before.

Morwen steps ahead. Checks the passage entrance. Nods back.

Clear.

You and Frizwick move Aldus toward the stairs. He tries to help. His legs find something approaching cooperation after the first few steps. Muscle memory surfacing slowly from wherever it went.

"Corven," you say. "He's alive."

Aldus makes a sound. Not words. Just pressure releasing somewhere deep.

"He came," Aldus says. After a moment. "To the cave mouth. Twice. Couldn't get through the seal." He keeps moving. Slow. "I heard him calling."

Three steps up. He manages the first one himself.

"He stopped coming," Aldus says. Flat. "Thought he'd given up. Or died."

Second step. Worse. You take more of the weight.

"He didn't give up," Frizwick says.

She doesn't elaborate. Neither do you.

The green light fades below as you climb. The blue-white of the channels picks up above. Aldus doesn't look back at the terminus stone.

That costs him something. You can see it.

He climbs anyway.

[FUTURE_EVENT_RESOLVED:Aldus Vareth must be returned to Corven per the party's word — his current condition complicates this.]

You take another step. Let him find his rhythm.

"The stone below," you say. "What do you know about it."

He thinks. Like recalling something he filed carefully against the possibility of needing it later.

"Drain," he says. "Not storage. I worked that out in the first month." A step. "The channels above feed it. Whatever they collect comes down and passes through. Out into the rock. Into the sea, I think."

"What does it collect."

"Intention," he says. Like that's a precise technical term. "Greed, specifically. The Thassilonians had a taxonomy. Greed as a force. Measurable. Harvestable." He pauses on a step. Breathing hard. "The mechanism above collects ambient resonance. The stone below disperses it safely. Two ends of one system."

Morwen, ahead, has gone very still. Listening.

"And when someone interrupts the dispersal end," she says without turning.

"The reservoir fills." Aldus doesn't hesitate. "Nualia was interfering with the intake above. Accelerating collection. Without the drain running at capacity."

He stops. Needs a moment.

"I kept the drain running," he says quietly. "Sitting against it. Contact maintained the connection. Kept it from backing up entirely."

Silence.

Two years against that stone. Keeping the mechanism balanced. Alone in the green dark.

Not incidental. Deliberate.

[LORE:Aldus Vareth maintained the terminus stone's dispersal function deliberately for two years, preventing the reservoir from reaching critical threshold. His presence was intentional caretaking, not accident.]

"Corven came to Sandpoint," you say. "Found us. Hired us to find you."

Aldus processes that. Slow blink.

"Hired," he says.

"Insisted," Frizwick corrects. Under her breath. But not that far under.

Another step. His legs are finding something closer to function. Still bad. Improving.

"He's been carrying a sketch," you say. "North face approach. Sea cave. Drawn it from memory." You think of the oilskin packet. The careful lines. "He knew the tides. Knew the approach. Kept it current."

Aldus says nothing for a while.

The stairs do the work of filling the silence.

"He never saw the inside," Aldus says finally. "The seal kept him out. He couldn't have known what it looked like in there."

"He didn't need to," you say. "He knew you were in it."

That lands.

Aldus stops on the step. Not because his legs failed. Different reason.

His jaw works once. The luminous eyes catch the blue-white from the channel walls and throw it back wrong.

"Two years," he says. Quiet. "He kept the sketch current for two years."

"Yes."

He starts climbing again. Faster than before. Like the information is fuel for something the mechanism never fed him.

Frizwick glances at you sideways. Says nothing.

Means something anyway.

"The caretaker upstairs explained the sequence," you say. "Four channels. Junction stone. But we need the drain end stable when we do it."

Aldus nods. Already thinking.

"Contact," he says. "Someone needs to maintain contact with the terminus stone during dispersal. When the reservoir releases it comes down fast. All at once." He pauses on a step. "The stone manages it. But it needs a conductor. A willing one."

"You."

"Was me," he says. "For two years, yes." He looks at his hands. The wrong temperature. The worn nails. "I don't know if I can do it again. Not immediately. Not in this condition."

Morwen speaks from ahead. "Does it have to be him specifically."

"No. Anyone willing. Aware of the terms." He glances back at you. "The stone reads intention. Same as the channels. Unwilling contact just gets burned."

You think of Daeris upstairs. Her river stone. Forty years of debt to something old and contractual. Her particular talent for sitting inside uncomfortable things without flinching.

Aldus reads something in your face.

"You have someone," he says.

Not a question.

"Maybe," you say.

He nods slowly. Considers.

"They need to know what they're agreeing to," he says. "The stone is specific about that. Informed. Willing. No coercion."

He almost smiles. Almost.

"It has standards."

"The thing at the junction," you say. "The caretaker. What do you know about it."

Aldus doesn't tense. Interesting.

"Old," he says. "Older than the mechanism. Older than Thassilon, I think." A step. "It visited me. Twice. Early on. Checked the connection. Confirmed I was maintaining contact deliberately." He pauses. "It seemed satisfied by that."

"Satisfied."

"Like a contractor confirming work is proceeding to specification." He finds that either faintly amusing or faintly terrible. Hard to tell. "It didn't linger. Didn't speak much. But it looked at the stone and then at me and something passed between us I can't properly describe."

"Try," Morwen says.

"Recognition," he says. "Like it had been waiting for someone to do this correctly. For a very long time."

You think of what Daeris read in the ward script. Voluntary service. Termination clause requiring outside hands. Ten thousand years alone at a junction stone waiting for someone to finish the work.

"Did it tell you about the contract," you say.

"No." Aldus frowns. "It asked me one question. First visit." He thinks. "It asked if I understood what I was sitting against."

"What did you say."

"I said not entirely. But I intended to learn." He exhales. "It left after that. Came back three months later. Didn't ask anything the second time."

Apparently that was answer enough.
